subject.title: openai-responses transport sends null content, rejected by strict providers (400 schema error)

question: Should maintainers accept source plus strict-mock SDK proof for a narrow OpenAI Responses `content: null` sanitizer, and should the implementation normalize null content to role-appropriate empty values before SDK send?
rationale: The current source and SDK types support the bug shape, but the only direct fix PR closed because no one with live strict-provider credentials supplied after-fix proof and no maintainer accepted the mock proof scope.

options.title: Accept narrow sanitizer with strict-mock proof
options.body: Allow a focused fix that replaces invalid null message content with role-appropriate empty values before Responses SDK sends, backed by source, SDK contract, and strict-provider mock regression tests.

options.title: Require live strict-provider proof first
options.body: Keep this issue blocked until the reporter or a maintainer with provider credentials captures redacted before/after logs from a strict OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint.

options.title: Choose a different normalization policy
options.body: Have an owner specify whether malformed null-content message items should be dropped or repaired differently before any new implementation PR is queued.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow sanitizer with strict-mock proof
recommendation.body: Allow a focused fix that replaces invalid null message content with role-appropriate empty values before Responses SDK sends, backed by source, SDK contract, and strict-provider mock regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent OpenAI Responses strict-provider work and co-authored post-hook payload hardening make this the best available proof-scope owner from the inspected history.
